lesson.text: Quick memory: what never mixes with electricity? (Water.) Today: spotting electricity dangers at home.
Electricity makes lights, toasters and tablets work. It travels along wires, and it can hurt, so it stays inside wires and machines.
Water and electricity never mix. Dry your hands before you touch a switch or a plug, and keep electric things far from the bath.
Nothing goes into a socket but a plug. Never poke anything into a socket or a toaster.
A cable with its wires showing, too many plugs in one socket, a kite in the power lines: don't touch. Tell a grown-up.
Try it in the world: open the practice house and find the dangers. Next: plugs, cables and power lines, on the Middle track.

exercises.prompt: Before you touch a light switch, your hands should be...
A hair dryer can sit on the edge of the bath.
exercises.explain: False: keep it far from the bath.

exercises.prompt: You see a cable with wires showing. You...
exercises.explain: Tell a grown-up, who switches it off.

exercises.prompt: You can poke a fork into the toaster to get the bread out.
exercises.explain: False: a grown-up unplugs it first.

exercises.prompt: Your kite is stuck in the power lines. You...
choices: leave it and tell a grown-up
exercises.hint: Power lines carry a lot of electricity.
exercises.explain: Leave it: the power company gets it down.
A plug and dry hands are safe; a drink and a fork are dangers.

exercises.prompt: Where is a safe place to fly a kite?
choices: an open field, far from power lines

exercises.prompt: Too many plugs in one socket can get too hot.
Found a danger? The right thing to do is...
Your hands are wet and you want the light on: put it in order.
exercises.explain: Dry your hands, then switch it on.
